newsitem.title: USA: Koch Metals sees summer start to LME trading.
newsitem.headline: Koch Metals sees summer start to LME trading.

text.p: Koch Metals Trading Ltd said it expected to start base metals trading in the summer as the company recruits from rivals that pulled back from the post-Sumitomo fray.
"The world has not stopped going round just because of Sumitomo," Frans Pettinga of Koch Metals said.
LME turnover has shrunk after the Japanese trading house lost $2.6 billion from copper dealings last year, traders said.

The new subsidiary of $30 billion a year Koch Industries, a privately-held company based in Wichita, Kansas, recruited Pettinga and David Sobotka, formerly of Lehman Brothers Commodities, and Jean-Luc Dubois, previously with J P Morgan's base metals business.
Lehman recently pulled out of ring dealing on LME, and Morgan has scaled down its London base metals operations.
Blue chip U.S. bank Morgan was also ticked off by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York for its role in financing activities of Sumitomo Corp's former maverick head copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka.
Although Koch (pronounced coke) is the second largest privately-traded company in the U.S., it is dipping its toes in the base metals pool for the first time.
Koch is not the only company to expand in base metals - recently GNI Group also boosted its operations in New York.
"I think there is quite a lot of room for an independent player with a good credit rating, good trading appetite and right people to make an impact on the market place," Pettinga said.
"There is a lot of pessimism around and a lot of people are struggling with the relics of days gone by," he added. "Koch

has traditionally invested in industries when perhaps they have been down in the dumps. The great strength of Koch is that is has the vision to look beyond the short-term, something which comes from being a private company," he added.
The company has applied to LME for category 2 membership which would allow it to do everything apart from deal in the ring, a step which Pettinga has not ruled out for a later date.

Koch has five staff and will build up to 12-15 by early next year. Dubois will head sales, probably from an office in energy-center Houston, with the other staff in London and, later on, in Singapore.
Much of the business will be focused on LME futures and options in the main base metals, along with over-the-counter products, and some physical-related dealings such as warrant financing.
The lack of strong producer ties rules out a major role in physical metals for now, Pettinga said.

Koch Metals hoped to see some cross over business tied to its parent's existing strong presence in petcoke and energy, two key ingredients in aluminum production, and sulphuric acid, a mining industry byproduct.
Koch is also one of the few companies to hedge PET, the plastic rival to aluminum in packaging.
Base metals trading was coming to grips with a new post-Sumitomo world, Pettinga said. Companies must handle their business professionally, be consistent and creditworthy, but not be risk averse.
